body:
FLiBe (2LiF·BeF₂) is the most promising molten salt for tritium breeding in the current literature, specifically in the Liquid Immersion Blanket configuration for compact high-field tokamaks, where its built-in Be neutron multiplier enables TBR ≥ 1.1 without enrichment and up to ~1.3 with Be-beryllide supplementation, while its low electrical conductivity avoids MHD penalties that disable competing liquid-metal designs.

*Why:* Be in FLiBe undergoes (n,2n) multiplication on fast neutrons, doubling the thermal neutron population available for ⁶Li(n,α)T breeding. The combined breeding and multiplication in a single fluid — without the need for separate multiplier structures — concentrates tritium production in the front 45 cm of the blanket where neutron flux is highest. Low electrical conductivity (~10⁻⁴ S/cm) suppresses magnetohydrodynamic pressure drop, allowing self-cooling in strong-field magnets where PbLi would be unworkable.

*Testable:*
- FLiBe with Be-beryllide pebbles at ~75–80 vol% multiplier fraction achieves TBR ≥ 1.3 in FNSF-class geometry without ⁶Li enrichment, while equivalent chloride salt configurations require both 90% ⁶Li enrichment and 90% ³⁷Cl enrichment to reach the same TBR.
- Chloride-salt candidates (LiCl-NaCl, LiCl-MgCl₂) exceed bare FLiBe TBR only when isotopically enriched (≥90% ⁶Li, ≥90% ³⁷Cl) and with a thicker blanket optimized for their longer neutron mean free path — unenriched chloride TBR remains ~0.6–0.7× FLiBe.
- FLiBe MHD pressure drop in a 12 T toroidal field blanket channel is at least one order of magnitude lower than an equivalent PbLi channel at the same flow velocity.
- Tritium permeation loss into structural steel walls scales inversely with tritium solubility; FLiBe's low tritium solubility predicts higher fractional permeation loss per unit surface area than PbLi, quantifiable in the BABY/LIBRA experiments as measurable T in the He cover gas within minutes of irradiation onset.

*Shaky:*
- Tritium solubility in FLiBe is extremely low, driving high tritium partial pressure and elevated permeation into structural materials — this is the single largest technical risk and no full-scale extraction demonstration exists.
- Be toxicity imposes severe handling and regulatory constraints, raising cost ($1,000–2,000/kg for FLiBe vs ~$360/kg for LiCl-based chlorides) and limiting industrial scalability.
- Materials compatibility database for fusion-relevant alloys in flowing FLiBe with magnetic fields and neutron flux is nearly empty; corrosion rates under realistic conditions are unknown.
- The TBR advantage of FLiBe over chloride salts is marginal or absent when chloride salts are isotopically enriched, meaning FLiBe's superiority is contingent on avoiding the cost of ⁶Li enrichment.

*Confidence* 0.62

## Verdict

**1. FLiBe (2LiF·BeF₂) is the most promising molten salt for tritium breeding in current fusion blanket literature, specifically in the Liquid Immersion Blanket configuration for compact high-field tokamaks, where its built-in Be neutron multiplier enables TBR ≥ 1.1 without enrichment and up to ~1.3 with Be-beryllide supplementation, while its low electrical conductivity avoids MHD penalties that disable competing liquid-metal designs.**

Beryllium in FLiBe undergoes (n,2n) neutron multiplication on fast neutrons, expanding the thermal neutron population available for ⁶Li(n,α)T reactions. This multiplication occurs within the same fluid that carries the bred tritium, concentrating production in the high-flux front ~45 cm of the blanket without separate multiplier structures. Low electrical conductivity (~10⁻⁴ S/cm) eliminates magnetohydrodynamic pressure-drop penalties that make liquid-metal (PbLi) blankets unworkable in strong-field (≥12 T) magnet environments.

*Standing.* Proposed but unreviewed. The Reviewer was budget-blocked before engaging, and the Proposer similarly could not respond. The hypothesis therefore survives the debate without having faced any objection — but that survival is vacuous: no prediction was tested, no mechanism was challenged, and no simulation was commissioned. The claim rests entirely on the Proposer's own framing of the literature (primarily FNSF/ARC LIB neutronics studies and MSR tritium-extraction work). Its internal tensions — particularly the conflict between high TBR and high tritium partial pressure driving permeation losses — were named by the Proposer but not resolved. The confidence is reduced from the Proposer's 0.62 to 0.45 to reflect that an unchallenged proposal in a budget-blocked debate has not been validated, and the open risks listed are substantial enough that a reviewer with access to the literature could plausibly overturn the ranking.
*Confidence.* 0.45

*Predictions.*
- FLiBe with Be-beryllide pebbles at ~75–80 vol% multiplier fraction achieves TBR ≥ 1.3 in FNSF-class geometry without ⁶Li enrichment.
- Chloride-salt candidates (LiCl-NaCl, LiCl-MgCl₂) reach equivalent TBR only when isotopically enriched to ≥90% ⁶Li and ≥90% ³⁷Cl with a thicker blanket; unenriched chloride TBR is ~0.6–0.7× FLiBe.
- FLiBe MHD pressure drop in a 12 T toroidal-field blanket channel is at least one order of magnitude lower than an equivalent PbLi channel at the same flow velocity.
- Tritium permeation loss into structural steel scales inversely with solubility; FLiBe's low tritium solubility produces measurably higher fractional permeation per unit surface area than PbLi, detectable as T in He cover gas within minutes of irradiation onset in BABY/LIBRA-class experiments.

**Why this order.** The debate produced exactly one substantive contribution: the Proposer's structured hypothesis. Both the Reviewer and the Proposer's second turn were budget-blocked before any argument was exchanged. The debate therefore ended with zero adversarial engagement. The hypothesis is ranked first by default — it is the only hypothesis — not because it prevailed against objections. Its standing reflects that reality: the claim is internally coherent and grounded in real neutronics literature, but its four testable predictions are untested within this thread, its three most serious risks (tritium permeation, Be toxicity at scale, corrosion data gap) are unresolved open questions acknowledged by the Proposer, and the conditional nature of FLiBe's advantage over enriched chloride salts was not probed. A prior debate on the same question ended without a verdict, and this one follows the same pattern. No consensus was reached; no consensus is reported.

**Unresolved.**
- Whether FLiBe's low tritium solubility produces permeation losses large enough to make tritium self-sufficiency impractical at reactor scale — settleable by a BABY/LIBRA-class flowing-loop irradiation experiment measuring T in He cover gas as a function of FLiBe surface-to-volume ratio and temperature.
- Whether isotopically enriched chloride salts (≥90% ⁶Li, ≥90% ³⁷Cl) match or exceed FLiBe TBR in an FNSF-class geometry — settleable by a salt-neutronics-tbr simulation comparing FLiBe LIB against LiCl-MgCl₂ at equivalent enrichment cost.
- What the corrosion rate of candidate structural alloys (316SS, Hastelloy-N, ODS steels) is in flowing FLiBe under simultaneous neutron flux and 12 T magnetic field at 600–700 °C — no experimental database currently covers this operating regime.
- Whether Be-beryllide pebble beds at 75–80 vol% fraction in an FLiBe LIB remain mechanically and chemically stable over a full reactor lifetime (~10 dpa He-equivalent), given that Be swelling data at fusion-relevant fluences is sparse.
- Whether the system-level tritium inventory and doubling time for an FLiBe LIB reactor is acceptable given the combination of high permeation rate and slow tritium extraction kinetics — this requires coupling the neutronics TBR to a tritium transport model with realistic permeation barriers, and has not been done for ARC/SPARC-scale parameters in any published source cited in this thread.
